qt: to the Commission Ioan-Rareş Bogdan (PPE) Subject:

The agreed 2027 EU budget sets EUR 57.1 billion aside for natural resources and the environment and caps direct payments to farmers at EUR 40.4 billion, which is less than the EUR 41-44 million average for 2014-2020. Because agricultural input inflation has outstripped the 30 % mark, the new budget’s payment cap is making the external convergence of direct payments a dead letter by stalling the alignment of direct per-hectare subsidies for farmers in Central and Eastern Europe. At the same time, of the EUR 75.7 billion allocated to the cohesion envelope, only EUR 58.4 billion have been earmarked for traditional projects. This is because resources that are supposed to reduce regional disparities have been diverted from basic infrastructure projects to fund parallel priorities (including defence, strategic technologies, and housing). I therefore ask the Commission: 1.
How will it ensure that the external convergence of direct payments for Eastern European farmers will be achieved under the new EUR 40.4 billion cap?
To what extent does the redirection of cohesion funds towards other priorities comply with the provisions of Article 174 TFEU on reducing regional disparities?
What compensatory mechanisms is it considering to counter the major erosion of agricultural and regional allocations caused by cumulative inflation?
